title: Specific evidence or general claims?
teaching_goal: Notice the difference between saying you have a quality and showing what you did.
question: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a colleague about how to do something.

rubric.label: What you did, step by step
What changed, and how you know

sentences.text: I'm a strong communicator, so disagreements don't usually last long with me.
Once a colleague and I disagreed about a project approach.
I listened to their side and explained mine, and we found a solution together.
In the end it worked out well and we learned a lot from each other.
On a team at a fictional delivery company, a colleague wanted to launch a new route-planning tool to all drivers at once.
I thought a two-week trial with one depot was safer, because the old tool had failed on rural addresses.
I asked for 20 minutes with her and brought three examples of failed rural deliveries from the last month.
We agreed to trial it at one depot first; the trial found the same rural-address problem, which was fixed before the wider launch.

explanation.summary: Answer B lets an interviewer see the disagreement, what the speaker did and what came of it. Answer A says the right things about itself, but almost nothing an interviewer could check or follow up.

strengths.why: Listening and explaining is a reasonable approach, and it's named.

gaps.why: A claim about yourself isn't evidence; the rest of the answer has to show it.
No details of what the disagreement was or what changed, so there's nothing to judge.

A.uncertain: It could be a true story told too briefly. A follow-up question would be needed to know.

strengths.why: The disagreement and the reason for it are concrete.
Specific actions: asked for time, brought examples.
A result that can be checked: the trial found the problem before launch.

gaps.why: It doesn't say how the working relationship went afterwards, which an interviewer might ask.

B.uncertain: Whether the colleague agreed willingly isn't said.

explanation.alternatives: Shorter answers can be fine when asked for one; what matters is that each sentence gives something checkable, not the length.

review_status: Written for practice with fictional details; checked for consistency, not reviewed by an outside interviewer.
